RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday,  the February 27, 2008/Phalguna 8, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Commerce and Industry; Defence; Earth Sciences; Home Affairs;
Information and Broadcasting; Labour and Employment; Parliamentary Affairs;
Rural Development; Science and Technology; Textiles)
Total number of questions — 20
7
Personnel of BSF leaving their jobs
*21. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SYEDA ANW ARA
TAIMUR:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than
40,000 personnel of Border Security Force
have left their jobs much before the
scheduled retirement during 2005-07;
(b) if so, whether a holistic study of
such large-scale exodus of trained para-
military personnel has been made; and
(c) whether sanctioned strength of
2,10,261 BSF personnel, available to guard
our borders, is adequate especially in view
of the belligerent neighbouring countries
across the borders?
Increasing working days under NREG
Scheme
†*22. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it has been made mandatory
to provide 100 working days employment
to a labourer under the National Rural
Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS);
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that 100
working days are not proving sufficient to
solve the financial predicament of labourers
in a year of 365 days;
(d) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto; and
(e) whether Government will consider
to increase the number of working days
from 100 to 150?
Implementation of Conditional Access
System
*23. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
put on hold the planned extension of the
Conditional Access System (CAS) to the
remaining areas of three of the four metros;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

8
(c) whether the CAS has failed in its
desired objectives in the areas where it has
been put into operation and if so, in what
aspects and to what extent?
Pashto service on AIR
*24. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of
INFORMATION AND BROAD-
CASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the All India
Radio (AIR) had Pashto service, which was
popular in Pashto speaking areas;
(b) if so, why was it discontinued and
since when;
(c) is there any proposal to restart it;
and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Digitization of EPF records
*25. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the
Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of employees
contributing to the Employees Provident
Fund (EPF) Account as on 31st March of
2001, year-wise till 2007 and the volume
of Provident Fund held in the corresponding
periods;
(b) whether Government had taken up
programme for digitization of the records
of Employees Provident Fund;
(c) if so, the details of the programme
indicating its origin, cost estimation and
potential benefits which complete
digitization would have accrued;
(d) the details of the progress made, so
far, in implementing the same, indicating
reasons for the delay, if any; and
(e) the time-frame presently fixed, if
any, for complete digitization of the PF
records?
Implementation of NREG scheme in
the whole country
†*26. SHRI SANJAY RAUT:
SHRI DATTA MEGHE:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has proposed
to implement the National Rural
Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS)
from April, 2008 in the whole country;
(b) if so, the steps taken for successful
implementation of this scheme;
(c) whether complaints have also been
received that irregularities are being
committed in the implementation of this
scheme; and
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government
to check irregularities in the implementation
of this scheme?
Resumption of arms supply to
Nepal
*27. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRI MAHMOOD A.
MADANI:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Nepal's Army Chief visited
New Delhi in December 2007, met Indian
leaders and made a pitch for India resuming
arms supplies to Nepal;
(b) if so, in what specific areas of arms
supplies, he sought Indian arms supplies;
and
(c) Government's response thereto?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

9
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
SEZs in Vidarbha region of
Maharashtra
†*28. SHRI DATTA MEGHE:
SHRI SANJAY RAUT:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Special Economic
Zones (SEZs) sanctioned for Maharashtra
and the number of SEZs, out of these, to be
set up in the Vidarbha region;
(b) the sectors of industry to which the
SEZs sanctioned for Vidarbha region in
Maharashtra belong to; and
(c) the steps taken by Government for
the development of those sectors?
Attack on North Indians in
Maharashtra
*29. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) and
its leader have recently launched a vicious
campaign and attack on 'North Indians'
living in Mumbai and other cities in
Maharashtra;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the number of people injured as a result of
unprovoked attacks by MNS;
(c) whether it is also a fact that leader of
MNS has not been arrested as yet despite
the fact that F.I.R. was registered against
him for encouraging attacks on North
Indians and if so, the reasons therefor; and
(d) whether any direction was issued to
the Maharashtra Government to bring the
culprits to book and, if so, with what result?
Rising crimes against women
*30. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the latest crime statistics
reportedly released by the National Crime
Records Bureau (NCRB) have shown that
every hour 18 women became victims of
crime and more than 7,618 women were
killed for dowry alone and that Delhi topped
the list of crime against women with 4,134
cases in 2006;
(b) if so, the details in this regard, State-
wise including crime against foreign tourists;
and
(c) the preventive measures so far taken
by Centre, in consultation with the State
Governments, to save India's image as well
as damage to the tourism industry?
Internal Security Scenario
*31. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
SHRIMA TI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Intelligence Bureau (IB) in
its report has pointed out a grim internal
security scenario across the country and
India is under the seize of terror threat which
could increase in the future;
(b) whether the alarming rise in the
casualties suffered by the security forces
both at the hands of maoists and terrorists
during 2007 increased and 179 security
personnel were killed in first 8 months of
2007 as against 100 in 2006;
(c) the other main features of the report;
and
(d) the concrete measures and steps
Government has taken to meet the security
threat in the country?

10
Security of women employees of
BPOs
*32. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
some women employees of certain BPOs
have been targeted and brutally murdered
and this heinous crime continues to spread
its tentacles;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government proposes to
put in place certain security measures/
guidelines for BPOs/other agencies
employing women to ensure safety and
security of their staff; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Inclusion of M/s MAS Holdings
Company under SITP
*33. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Andhra Pradesh
Government has requested the Union
Government for inclusion of M/s MAS
Holdings Company under the Scheme for
Integrated Textile Projects (SITP) to provide
with requisite financial support for
development of common infrastructure in
the Integrated Textile Park;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reasons for delay in giving
clearance to this proposal; and
(d) by when clearance is likely to be
given?
Salt production
   †*34. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
 SHRI RAJ MOHINDER SINGH
MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
production of salt is on the decrease
continuously in the last few years in the
country;
(b) if so, the decrease recorded in the
production of salt from the year 2005 to
2008; and
(c) the amount of hike in the price of
salt in the country due to such shortage?
Special package for importers affected
by rupee appreciation
*35. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHA V AN:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry is considering
any special package to importers who
suffered losses due to the rise in the value
of rupee;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether the Ministry will
recommend such packages for NRIs who
also suffered set-backs due to the
unprecedented rise of rupee?
Attack on Hindi speaking people in
Maharashtra
†*36. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Maharashtra
Navnirman Sena (MNS) has issued a dictate
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

11
to non-Maharashtrian people, particularly
belonging to Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and other
people, entrepreneurs and labourers of
other Hindi speaking States asking them to
leave Maharashtra;
(b) whether it is also a fact that non-
Maharashtrian people were beaten in
Mumbai, Kalyan, Thane and other cities
from the first week of February, 2008, their
shops were looted and they were dragged
from trains, buses and taxis and insulted
and beaten; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and
Government's point of view in this
regard?
Research made by
CSIR
*37. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of SCIENCE AND
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether country is lagging behind
several countries in different fields of science
and technologies such as nano-technology,
bio-technology, plasma physics, robotics
and laser physics;
(b) if so, the steps taken/proposed to
be taken by the Council for Scientific and
Industrial Research (CSIR) for research in
the above fields and the amount spent in
each of the above fields and achievements
made during the each of the last three years
by CSIR;
(c) whether the outcome of the research
is not commensurate with the amount spent
by it;
(d) if so, the steps contemplated in this
regard; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Constitution of Police Accountability
Commission
*38. SHRIMA TI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is considering
a proposal to constitute a Police
Accountability Commission in order to
probe public complaints against the police
for serious misconduct; and
(b) if so, the details in this regard and
by when the Commission is likely to be
constituted?
Prohibiting employment of
children
*39. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of list of hazardous
processes and occupations where
employment of children below 18 years is
strictly prohibited;
(b) whether it is a fact that the Ministry
proposes to expand the list of hazardous
processes and occupations; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Violation of child labour
law
†*40. SHRI PYARELAL KHANDEL-
W AL: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
child labour is still existing in various States
in the country and labour laws are being
openly flouted;
(b) if so, the States in the country from
where child labourers have been rescued
during the last one year; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

12
(c) the action taken against the persons
found responsible for violation of labour
laws during the last one year, the details
thereof, State-wise?
NEW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 21st February, 2008 Secretary-General.
Phalguna 2, 1929 (Saka)

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Commerce and Industry : 28, 34, 35,
Defence : 27,

Information and Broadcasting : 23, 24,
Labour and Employment : 25, 39, 40,

Textiles : 33.
13
